title: How Online Gambling Works
summary: Josh Clark and Chuck Bryant explore online gambling: hosts share personal experiences with free-play and sports betting, then trace its history from Antigua and Barbuda's 1994-era licensing law and early Microgaming software, through the late-1990s/2000s online poker boom (Party Poker, Poker Stars, Chris Moneymaker's 2003 World Series of Poker win), the US crackdown (Wire Wire Act, UIGEA 2006, Black Friday 2011), and the Obama-era Justice Department reversal allowing state-regulated online gambling. They discuss differences between online and casino play, payment processing and withdrawal issues, state geolocation-based online gambling in New Jersey, Nevada, and Delaware, daily fantasy sports like DraftKings and FanDuel, the risks of rigged or shady sites and addiction, and sports-betting scandals. The episode ends with listener mail from Brazil praising the show.

segments.title: History of online gambling beginnings
segments.summary: Antigua and Barbuda passed the Free Trade and Processing Act in the mid-1990s, creating licenses for online casinos. Microgaming produced early online gaming software, and online casinos spread worldwide, with the US left out.

segments.title: Antigua WTO dispute and early online sports betting and poker
segments.summary: Hosts describe the World Trade Organization ruling in Antigua's favor against the US and sanctions, then early sports wagering via Betfair and the late-1990s/early-2000s online poker boom, including Chris Moneymaker's 2003 World Series of Poker win after online qualifying.
